draft.title: Algorithms that sort shapes
card: An algorithm is a set of steps to follow in order. A sorting algorithm uses yes or no questions to put shapes into groups.
A flowchart shows this. Each question sits in a box with two exits, Yes and No. A shape follows the exits until it reaches a group.
Example: Question 1 is 'Does it have 4 sides?' If No, the shape goes to the group 'Not a quadrilateral'. If Yes, Question 2 is 'Does it have 4 equal sides?'

A square has 4 sides, so it answers Yes to Question 1. It has 4 equal sides, so it answers Yes to Question 2 and goes to the group 'Equal sides'. A rectangle that is not a square answers No to Question 2 and goes to the other group.
draft.remember: Follow the yes or no answers one question at a time to reach the shape's group.

a.q: Using the flowchart in the card, which group does a triangle end up in?
opts: It does not reach a group
a.why: A triangle has 3 sides, so the answer to Question 1 is No. That sends it straight to 'Not a quadrilateral'. It never reaches Question 2, so it cannot go to 'Equal sides'.
a.clue: Count the sides of a triangle and answer Question 1.

b.q: Mia sorts shapes with this flowchart: Q1 'Does it have 4 sides?' Yes goes to Q2, No goes to 'Other'. Q2 'Are all 4 sides equal?' Yes goes to 'Group A', No goes to 'Group B'. Where does a rectangle that is not a square go?
b.why: A rectangle has 4 sides, so Q1 is Yes and it moves to Q2. Its sides are not all equal because it is not a square, so Q2 is No and it goes to Group B. Group A is tempting because a rectangle has 4 sides, but only shapes with all sides equal go there.
b.clue: Answer Q1 first, then Q2, using the shape's sides.
